lines.text: Ada and Ben both have a workspace called storefront, and both are working on the same shop.
Until now, they were two islands. Neither could see what the other agent was doing.
Sometimes both agents even edit the same file, and nobody finds out until the merge conflict.
In Agent R Q, when two teammates share workspaces with the same name, it becomes one team workspace.
There is nothing to configure. The two merge into one, and both of them stay in control of their own agents.
Now both see each other's tasks live, each one marked with the owner's name.
So Ada notices that Ben is already fixing the signup email, and she picks something else.
The agents read each other's memory too. Ben's agent leaves a note about a quirky test, and Ada's agent can read it.
Each agent only writes to its own memory. Teammates can read it, but never change it.
Nothing is shared until each person chooses it. Share a skill, or keep it private.
One project, one shared view, and a team that finally knows what is going on.
Name them the same, and join the islands. Try teams at Agent R Q dot com.
